acceptance.behavior: Google OAuth starts from /login, returns through /auth/callback, and reaches canonical onboarding or the existing profile's OS route.
The responsive login and signup modes expose an accessible Google action, busy state, and announced recoverable failure state.
The callback persists a canonical verified profile for the authenticated Google identity and rejects persistence failure.
A new Google identity may carry a normalized public signup role while an existing profile's role and onboarding state remain authoritative.
The acceptance spec writes the required exact-revision screenshots, trace, accessibility report, and PBOS result manifest.
One Playwright journey validates OAuth initiation, callback persistence, authority routing, desktop, mobile, accessibility, and exact-revision artifacts.
The Google action has visible text and busy semantics, and the mobile route rejects serious or critical axe violations.
Callback errors are non-enumerating, role handoff is limited to new Google identities, and failed profile persistence signs out the session.
